chunks: Ahmad ibn Ziyad ibn Ja'far al-Hamadani (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd al-Yaqtini narrated to us, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from al-Hasan ibn Ziyad, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) that he said:

Whoever gives charity in Sha'ban, Allah the Mighty and Majestic will nurture it for him just as one of you nurtures his young camel, until he arrives on the Day of Resurrection and it has become for him the like of Mount Uhud.

key_terms.أحد: Uhud — a prominent mountain near Medina, site of the Battle of Uhud; used here to signify enormous magnitude
key_terms.شعبان: Sha'ban — the eighth month of the Islamic calendar, immediately preceding Ramadan, considered a month of special spiritual significance
key_terms.صدقة: Sadaqah — voluntary charity or alms given for the sake of God
key_terms.فصيل: Fasil — a young camel (foal), used metaphorically to illustrate growth and nurturing

ai.seo_question: What is the reward of giving charity in the month of Sha'ban?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) teaches that charity given during the month of Sha'ban receives extraordinary divine multiplication. Using the vivid analogy of nurturing a young camel until it grows, he explains that God will cause such charity to grow until the Day of Resurrection, when its reward will be as massive as Mount Uhud. This teaching was delivered in the context of encouraging believers to take advantage of the sacred months preceding Ramadan.
word_analysis: may He have mercy on him

en.bilal-muhammad: Ahmad b. Ziyad b. Ja`far al-Hamadani (rh) narrated to us. He said: `Ali b. Ibrahim b. Hashim narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. `Isa b. `Ubayd al-Yaqtini narrated to us from Yunus b. `Abd al-Rahman from al-Sadiq Ja`far b. Muhammad (as). He said:
Whoever gives charity in Sha`ban, Allah will nurture it just as one of you nurtures a child; until it becomes the like of [Mount] Uhud on the Day of Resurrection.
